title: Topological Band Theory for High-Dimensional Parameter Spaces
authors: Vivek Chakrabhavi, Walt Chavarria, Jonathan J. Heckman, Steven Rayan
abstract: We study the topological band theory of quantum Hall systems in which the adiabatic flux parameters of an external gauge potential form a high-dimensional manifold. This situation arises both for strongly correlated matter on spatial Riemann surfaces of genus $g > 1$, as well as in the formal study of matter on compact oriented manifolds of dimension $4\ell+2 = 2p$ coupled to $p$-form gauge potentials. In these cases, the underlying topological invariants defined over the parameter space are significantly richer than the low-dimensional (i.e., two-dimensional) case and involve both the curvature (i.e., first Chern class) as well as higher order curvature invariants. These higher curvature invariants correspond to topologically protected contributions to Kubo-like formulae, constructed from correlation functions of the physical current operators. We illustrate these general considerations with an explicit example from hyperbolic band theory based on the genus-two Bolza Riemann surface, a case which has recently been simulated on a synthetic-dimension platform.
summary: This work extends topological band theory beyond the standard 2D quantum Hall effect by analyzing systems on high-dimensional parameter spaces or curved manifolds. It shows that the topological invariants are governed by higher-order curvature terms, generalizing the Chern number concept. This provides a robust theoretical tool for characterizing topological phases in complex, higher-dimensional physical settings.
main_problem: The paper generalizes topological band theory, traditionally applied to 2D quantum Hall systems, to systems defined on high-dimensional parameter spaces or curved manifolds.
main_result: The topological invariants generalize from the Chern class to higher-order curvature invariants involving the symplectic form and the Berry curvature, leading to quantized contributions in Kubo-like formulae.
method: The theory constructs a Berry connection and curvature on the high-dimensional parameter space $M_\Theta$, generalizing the standard integral quantization procedures.
model_or_system: The study considers quantum Hall systems on Riemann surfaces of genus $g>1$ or matter on compact oriented manifolds of dimension $4\ell+2$. The analysis uses hyperbolic band theory as an explicit example.
key_observables:
Generalized Hall conductivity $\sigma_{Hall}$ and higher integral invariants $
u_m$, which are quantized integers.
important_parameters: The dimension of the parameter space ($d>2$) and the genus of the underlying manifold ($g>1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis requires defining the symplectic form $S$ on the moduli space $M_\Theta$ and retaining the full differential-geometric data on the parameter space.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the Brillouin zone for a square lattice as a quotient torus $T^2$. Other figures relate to the geometry of the parameter space and background gauge potentials.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the standard 2D case, then generalizing the theory to higher dimensions using background $p$-form potentials, and finally illustrating the general framework with a concrete example on the genus-two Bolza Riemann surface.
why_interesting: The generalization of topological invariants to higher dimensions and curved spaces provides a powerful mathematical framework applicable to modern condensed matter systems beyond simple lattice models.
